notes: Steps A-F complete. The open question - which ropivacaine concentrations stayed clear after the bicarbonate addition - is answered with a negative: none, because only two were tested. Ropivacaine was put through the initial titration at its two strongest commercial strengths, precipitated above pH 6.0 and was excluded before the main experiment, so it never reached the point the paper's Table 1 reports for the other six solutions; no weaker ropivacaine strength was tested at all. The Results sentence about no precipitate in 'any of the local anaesthetic solutions' covers the six carried through (three bupivacaine strengths, two bupivacaine-with-epinephrine, one lidocaine-with-epinephrine), not ropivacaine. On Milner alone D017 stays confirmed; the companion full text Ramos 2001 (S-686-24) refutes it, and the two D017 entries are written to be read together - a worker merging the two files will see one 'confirmed' and one 'refuted' entry for the same claim, and the Ramos entry is the deciding one.
